question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\frac{4}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\frac{4}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[4\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y]_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}4\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}4x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}4x\,dx & ={[2{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =2{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16} \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
